title: Secondary School Certificate Class X Model Examination Paper 2027 and Onwards — Chemistry Paper III (Practical)
objective: To demonstrate the methods of removing calcium ions from the given hard water samples A and B.

tasks.prompt: Set the apparatus and perform the experiment. Do not write the method. (Examiner’s observation)
tasks.solution: Student correctly takes hard water sample A in test tube 1, adds lime water Ca(OH)2 dropwise until precipitation occurs, filters off precipitate; takes sample B in test tube 2, adds Na2CO3 solution, observes precipitation, and filters.

tasks.prompt: Which substances are responsible for the permanent hardness of water?
tasks.solution: Dissolved chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium, such as CaCl2, CaSO4, MgCl2, and MgSO4.

tasks.prompt: Why is it essential to remove hardness from water?
tasks.solution: Hard water wastes excessive soap by forming insoluble curd/scum, causes scale and boiler incrustation in industrial steam boilers (reducing heat transfer efficiency and causing boiler explosions), and clogs hot water pipes.

tasks.prompt:
Write what happens when you perform the tests given in the table below. Draw an inference from your observations.

1. Sample of hard water A + lime water [Ca(OH)2]
2. Sample of hard water B + sodium carbonate solution
tasks.solution:
| Obs. # | Test | Observation | Type of Hardness Removed |
| :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Sample of hard water A + lime water [Ca(OH)2] | A milky white precipitate forms | Temporary hardness |
| 2 | Sample of hard water B + sodium carbonate solution | A white precipitate forms | Permanent hardness |

tasks.prompt: Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction between sample of hard water A and lime water.
Evaluation of student practical laboratory notebook and continuous assessment record.
tasks.solution: 2 Marks awarded for complete, verified, and signed practical journal records.
